02 / TRAJECTORY

An inland-to-sea
hypersonic profile

The interceptor cold-launches vertically at 40.0°N / 110.0°E and climbs south-east; the target enters head-on at Mach 2.0 from 28.0°N / 126.0°E at 15 km altitude.

03 / ENERGY & ATTITUDE

Energy management and attitude response

Boost peak dynamic pressure is about 0.31 MPa and the cruise settles at 20–22 km; the three-loop autopilot tracks the guidance command with all four fins inside their deflection limits.

04 / GUIDANCE & HANDOVER

Handover gates and endgame geometry

At 637.3 s the range, altitude difference, speed, lead angle, seeker lock and available-load gates are all satisfied; midcourse cross-fades to terminal guidance and the intercept closes with a 61.1 m miss distance.

05 / METHOD & DATA

Simulation setup and reading guide

All metrics come from one fixed-step 5 ms RK4 digital flight with 47 telemetry columns and 61,992 frames. The curves are evenly sampled at 900 points; key metrics are computed from the full data set.

How to read this report

Miss distance is not the last-frame range but the zero crossing of the range rate as it turns from negative to positive, which avoids the fly-by distortion that a ~3 km/s closing speed would otherwise cause.

Load-factor curves compare the guidance command with the actual non-gravity acceleration. The 40 g endgame value is the command limit, not a structural load; the actual load is bounded by dynamic pressure and fin effectiveness.

Seeker off-boresight angle exceeds the FOV during long-range midcourse (11.4% of samples), but the handover window satisfies the lock condition; the LOS angle converges inside 10° in terminal guidance.

  • ECI is the primary frame; the Earth is a 6371 km sphere and aerodynamics uses air-relative velocity.
  • Thrust is altitude-corrected as F = F_sl + A_e(P_sl − P_a).
  • Mass is floored at dry mass; thrust is zero once propellant is exhausted.

Data note
This report is generated from telemetry.csv for algorithm and software verification only. Complete public data for a 2000-km-class interceptor are scarce; the geometry, mass, aerodynamics and propulsion parameters are engineering extrapolations from public sources and generic hypersonic-vehicle characteristics, and do not represent any in-service system.

References

  1. PyDATCOM / datcom-parser — aero coefficients and DATCOM axis mapping.
  2. JAST-Bezier — Mohamadifard & Naghash, JAST Vol.8 No.2.
  3. ZEM/APN — ZEM/APN terminal-guidance survey (Evduzen, 2026) and the standard PN/APN literature.
  4. Hacettepe-3loop / TU-Delft-AW — three-loop attitude control, anti-windup and gain scheduling.
  5. gnss-ins-sim — GNSS/INS noise levels; DTIC-Glint — glint model.
  6. USSA1976 — NASA-TM-X-74335 standard atmosphere.
